text.p: Following are some of the major events which occurred on September 21 in history.
19 BC - Virgil, great epic Roman poet, died. Full name Publius Vergilius Maro best known for his unfinished epic the Aeneid.
1327 - King Edward II of England was murdered in Berkeley Castle, and was succeeded by his son Edward III.
1415 - Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor 1452-93, born. Largely responsible for uniting the various Habsburg domains in Europe into the powerful House of Habsburg.
1452 - Girolamo Savonarola, Italian reformer and member of the Dominican Order, born. He drove Pietro de Medici from power and became leader of Florence 1494-97.
1645 - Louis Joliet, French-Canadian who explored the northern portions of the Mississippi River, the Hudson Bay and Labrador coast, born.
1745 - The Battle of Prestonpans took place in Scotland, in which the Jacobite army under Bonnie Prince Charlie gained a victory over English Royal forces led by Sir John Cope.
1756 - John Loudon McAdam, Scottish engineer and inventor of the macadam road surface, born.
1784 - The Pennsylvania Packet and Daily Advertiser was published to become the first successful daily newspaper in the United States.
1792 - The monarchy was abolished in France, a day before the country was declared a republic.
1832 - Sir Walter Scott, Scottish novelist and poet notably of "Ivanhoe" and "Talisman", died aged 61.

1866 - H(erbert) G(eorge) Wells, English author whose first work "The Time Machine" pioneered science fiction, born. Best remembered for "War of the Worlds", his vision of a Martian invasion of Earth.
1867 - Henry Lewis Stimson, U.S. Secretary of War, 1911-13 and 1940-45, born. He made a recommendation to President Harry Truman that atomic bombs should be dropped on Japan.
1874 - Gustav Theodore Holst, English composer of Swedish descent best known for his orchestral suite "The Planets", born.
1909 - Kwame Nkrumah, Ghanaian statesman, born. He was the country's first prime minister, and president of the republic.
1931 - Larry Hagman, U.S. actor and director, born. Son of singer and actress Mary Martin (of "South Pacific" fame) he will always be identified with the "JR' character in the TV series "Dallas'.
1931 - Britain abandoned the gold standard.
1934 - Leonard Cohen, Canadian poet-turned-singer, born. Noted for melancholy lyrics, he was popular in the 1960's and made a comeback in the late 1980's.
1947 - Stephen King, US novelist, born. Author of "Carrie", "The Shining" and other horror stories.
1957 - King Haakon VII of Norway died and was succeeded by his son Olav V.
1964 - Malta became independent after 164 years of British rule.
1965 - The Gambia, the Maldives and Singapore were admitted to the United Nations.
1976 - Former Chilean cabinet minister Orlando Letelier was killed in Washington D.C., by a bomb placed in his car.
1978 - Nigeria's rulers announced a new constitution and lifted a ban on political parties which had been in effect since 1966.
1990 - Marshal Xu Xiangqian, a former Chinese defence minister and veteran of the Communist revolution, died aged 88.
1990 - Nicu Ceausescu, flamboyant playboy son of the late Romanian communist dictator, was jailed for 20 years.
1992 - The Vatican and Mexico established full diplomatic relations, ending a rift of 130 years.
1993 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin dissolved parliament and called elections after the defiant assembly sought to strip him of his powers and swore in Alexander Rutskoi as acting president.
1995 - Russian commandos stormed a hijacked bus, freeing 18 hostages and arresting two gunmen in a lightning raid.
